answer: Each identity must hold one radio cell, or clones stay cheap. A candidate locks 12.8 POA and draws one 40 m tundra square from the epoch seed, then buries a 0.64 kg crystal stake whose cut stays hidden until second 8. For nine minutes they send one 19-bit pulse at 437.15 MHz; two polar clocks accept only a 2.86-3.02 ms echo and error under 18 Hz. Ninety aliases would freeze 1,152 POA and need ninety exclusive squares. Auditors recompute the cell and replay the cut from the seed. A reused square, copied pulse, or echo off by more than 0.09 ms burns 43% and ices that cell for seven epochs.
